newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek registered unemployment at 9.27 pct in Jan.
newsitem.headline: Greek registered unemployment at 9.27 pct in Jan.

text.p: Greece's January registered unemployment rose to 9.22 percent from December's 8.42 percent and 9.22 percent a year ago, the labour ministry said in a statement.
The number of unemployed stood at 225,688 in January, roughly unchanged from 225,944 in the same month in 1996. But the number of employed fell by 85,299 to 2,207,619, it said.
New hirings stood at 35,504 in January, outpacing layoffs of 26,676 and reflecting the lack of uniform hiring/layoff patterns among firms, it said.
Greece's registered unemployment rate is known to be lower than the actual unemployment.

Workers can stay on state unemployment payrolls for a period spanning five to 12 months depending on the amount of daily wages in the last year of employment, which also determines their daily subsidy.
Workers are entitled to a one-off bonus if they continue to remain unemployed after the maximum 12-month period.
They are dropped out of the unemployment roll if they find a job or stop showing up at Organisation for Human Resources (OAED) branches. The unemployed are obliged to show up once per month at OAED.

About 1.2 trillion drachmas ($4.5 billion) of EU funds have been earmarked for training and relocation programmes for the unemployed for the period 1996-2000, but Greece has absorbed about 10 percent of the total sum so far, labour experts said.

"In a bid to increase the absorption rate of EU funds, the labour authorities have classified university graduates who have not had a job before as unemployed and admit them to these programmes," the expert said.
University graduates searching for their first job were not classified as unemployed or as part of the labour force in the past, he said.
"This is one of the reasons that has registered unemployment underestimate actual unemployment by a big margin in the past, perhaps more than two percent," the expert said.
The National Statistics Service (NSS) also releases an unemployment figure based on the results of its annual survey. The survey is based on sampling and seems to better mirror actual unemployment.
NSS has yet to release the unemployment rate for 1996.
The number of unemployed rose to 10 percent of the labour force in 1995 against 9.6 percent in 1994 according to past NSS surveys.

The national economy ministry forecasts a dip in the unemployment rate to 9.8 percent in 1996 and another drop to 9.6 percent in 1997. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4 ($ = 264.7 Greek Drachmas)
